scope: Current standalone design prototype, planning and decision flow

steps.observed: Visit names, time windows and generic unknown checkboxes are visible; meal, hotel, transport completeness and a recommendation rationale are not presented in the day context.
steps.direction: Show the day as an understandable travel plan, with traveler fit, paced sequence, missing arrangements and specific next actions.

steps.observed: Two broad areas are described separately; straight-line distance, unknown costs and unverified access do not establish the outcome of switching.
steps.direction: Compare concrete equivalent options with one recommendation, meaningful tradeoffs, source/estimate states and the change to the rest of the day.

steps.observed: Fourteen unknown acknowledgments dominate the review; the user must leave to inspect local conditions and cannot assess a whole-trip decision from this screen.
steps.direction: Summarize the plan being adopted, budget coverage, unresolved practical decisions and exact follow-up coverage; preserve contextual individual acknowledgments.

steps.observed: The form explicitly updates only one visit and leaves overlap resolution to the user. It does not preview connected timing, transport or cost changes.
steps.direction: Decide the propagation behavior with the user, then design a before/after impact preview that protects booked and locked items.

limits: Design prototype and synthetic data only; no production adoption or external action was performed.
This audit used the current desktop pane; mobile behavior and full accessibility were not assessed.
Only opening, comparing, reviewing and opening the time form were performed; no inputs or itinerary choices were saved.
